@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+O7 is blocked at the required stall-profile prerequisite. No O7 candidate has been implemented or built, and no performance result or break-even is claimed.
+
+NEEDS-BOX: schedule overlap-O7 for baseline stall attribution on the 25GbE two-netns rig, initially GET/SET p32 in both 1s and 2s with read-local, atomic, key-lb and client-lb all 1, overlap 0/1 compared separately, and reorder held fixed. Assign server/load-generator CPUs entirely within 0-111 and an owned port. No measurement slot was granted during this turn.
+
+The inspected checkout is `/home/user/Projects/cx-overlap-O7`, branch `cx-overlap-O7`, commit `87b88cc4eb7d791c87b83a43215454d38c0f72f8`. The competition brief and history were read in the requested order. This report is under ignored `build/` and stays out of git.
+
+The prerequisite is explicit in the task: "Prove which with a stall profile before building." A throughput plateau alone cannot distinguish reply retirement, request publication/wakeup, executor storage stalls, or load-generator limits. The task also explicitly reserves box scheduling to the maintainer. No server, load generator, benchmark, gate, compiler, perf capture, or process termination was run.
+
+The archived evidence inspected does not satisfy the prerequisite:
+
+| Evidence | Recorded conditions | Limit for O7 |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `../cx-cacheutil/scratchpad/cacheutil/ibs-results.md` | Six operation-count IBS captures; split GET/MGET/SET at read-local 0; LB and atomic off; all split cells unsaturated | These are sampled demand-access/type counts, not an armed stall attribution of the current reply crossing. The report explicitly does not quote cycles/op from these captures. |
+| `../cx-cacheutil/CACHEUTIL.md` | Older `bebfde2997` checkout; 12-worker geometry; provisional/co-tenanted measurements | The layout candidate measurements do not establish a current O7 reply bottleneck. |
+| `../cx-ovldesign-b/OVERLAPDESIGN.md` | Older `bebfde2997` checkout; loopback; both LBs off in mechanism experiments | Records reply fragmentation and SEND/op effects, but is not armed NIC stall evidence. It also records measured GETs taking the local lane, with owner work confined to preload. |
+
+The current source already has parts of the proposed overlap. These observations are static, not measured bottleneck claims:
+
+| Boundary | Current source | Consequence for the required attribution |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Split publication | `src/core/io_loop.h:4351`, `src/core/thread.h:490` | Quiet task pushes publish queue data before IFID.POST. IFID.POST publishes the notification bit and decides the wake. Moving it cannot be described as first making task data visible. |
+| Split shallow schedule | `src/core/iopipe_pipeline.h:93`, `src/core/io_loop.h:5551` | WB observe/prefetch, IFID parse/hash, WB retire/prepare, IFID post, WB submit. Reply preparation currently precedes the notification/wake stage, but new tasks are already published. A sleeping executor and a polling executor are different cases. |
+| Split deep schedule | `src/core/io_loop.h:5560` | IFID parse/post precedes WB gather/serve. It already permits new owner work to run concurrently with IO retirement. Extra staging needs evidence of a remaining gap. |
+| Executor reply completion | `src/core/ex_loop.h:2935`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:2999` | Done publication, ready-mask notification and wake decisions already have batch aggregation. Removing the Done-to-ready fence would reintroduce the lost-wakeup defect documented at this site. |
+| Fused overlap | `src/core/io_loop.h:4949`, `src/core/ex_loop.h:2000` | A synchronous WB callback already runs in the first held owner batch's prefetch gap. A fused thread cannot execute ordinary CPU instructions from two batches simultaneously; its benefit must come from hiding latency, not asserting additional parallel cores. |
+| Local reads | `src/core/io_loop.h:5434`, `src/core/rl2s.cc:335` | Armed split IO drains its local-read lane. Per-thread local-hit counters are available to distinguish local work from owner-routed work. Armed GET is not automatically a witness of the EX-to-IO reply crossing. |
+
+One pre-existing correctness risk needs maintainer attention before any wider WB interleave. The call chain is present in this checkout; no runtime counterexample was attempted:
+
+1. `ExLoopT::drain_tasks_with_filler` holds an unexecuted stack batch and calls the WB filler after prefetch (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2014`).
+2. The filler calls `prepare_pipeline`; `WbEngine::serve_impl` invokes the retirement hook for special state (`src/core/io_loop.h:5059`, `src/net/wb.h:802`).
+3. The hook can retire a completed EXEC. `multi_retire` executes its IO-local child handlers, including BGSAVE (`src/core/io_loop.h:116`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:1708`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:2070`, `src/cmd/t_server.cc:638`).
+4. Snapshot start calls `writer.progress_fused_executor()` during preparation/freeze/mark (`src/snapshot/snapshot.cc:284`). With overlap armed this hook calls `fused_coarse_pass()` on the same executor (`src/core/genthread.cc:203`).
+5. That re-enters task draining while the older outer batch is still held. The ordinary drain takes queue entries before execution and retires them around its callback (`src/core/thread.h:609`). The pre-filler exceptional-state check only sees snapshot state that already existed before the callback (`src/core/ex_loop.h:463`); a BGSAVE started inside the callback is later than that check.
+
+The resulting concern is that younger work, including later work on the same connection, can be drained while earlier work remains in the outer batch. That is an ordering/RYOW and snapshot-cut risk, not a complaint about unrelated cross-client ordering. It needs a directed counterexample that forces this callback and proves the window opened. The earlier overlap-design report independently records guarding MULTI clients against this same recursion; its guard is not present in the current WB capture/filler shown above. No unrelated fix or speculative guard was added in O7.
+
+For the scheduled prerequisite, preserve separate evidence for these candidate causes:
+
+- IO reply preparation: sampled locations in `wb_retire_prepare`, `wb_serve_natural`, `WbEngine::serve_impl`, ROB Done-state loads, reply materialization and borrowed-value copies.
+- Request/completion crossing: task notification and ready-mask accesses, queue/ROB pressure, executor and IO wake/park activity, and per-role scheduled time. CPU busy time is not proof of useful progress; memory stalls are not sleep time.
+- Storage/local execution: sampled locations and load latency for bucket/record accesses, with per-thread read-local hit deltas identifying the actual command path.
+- Send/kernel work: SEND/command, commands/SEND, bytes/command, short-write/backpressure and io_uring/kernel samples. Loopback cannot establish the requested send-path claim.
+
+Use existing witnesses and instruments first: `INFO SERVER` exposes overlap passes/interleaved passes (`src/core/orthog.h:49`) and per-thread local hits; existing WB/network and LBSIGNALS reporting covers retirement/sends/wakes. `tests/abba_profile.py` already supplies per-server-TID cycles/instructions/ref-cycles and schedstat accounting. Its own contract says PMC windows encompass the command interval and per-command ratios are approximate; it is not an instruction-address stall sampler or exact alignment proof. The archived IBS decoder/accounting helpers can be reused for sampled-access evidence. Keep unknown attribution and lost/throttled samples explicit; sampled memory latency is not an additive count of wall-clock stalled cycles.
+
+Record current executable digest/build ID, complete argv, actual worker TIDs/roles/affinity, generator geometry and offered load, populated-hit evidence and the command-count interval. If reproducing a correctness gate row, preserve its explicit 16 shards and assigned GATE_RATIO/GATE_CORES (default 0-7, 6:2). The ABBA instrument derives its own shard count (`tests/abbagate.py:1146`); do not silently equate that geometry to a correctness gate boot. Capture stall diagnostics separately from unprofiled verdict runs so sampling perturbation is visible.
+
+PRE/POST status is below. Every metric is unavailable: no qualifying current PRE capture was obtained and no POST candidate exists. An empty table is not treated as a passing comparison. Tuples are `(rate, IPC, instr/command, cycles/command)`; MGET/MSET count commands, not individual keys.

+1. `ExLoopT::drain_tasks_with_filler` holds an unexecuted stack batch and calls the WB filler after prefetch (`src/core/ex_loop.h:2014`).
+2. The filler calls `prepare_pipeline`; `WbEngine::serve_impl` invokes the retirement hook for special state (`src/core/io_loop.h:5059`, `src/net/wb.h:802`).
+3. The hook can retire a completed EXEC. `multi_retire` executes its IO-local child handlers, including BGSAVE (`src/core/io_loop.h:116`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:1708`, `src/cmd/multi.inc:2070`, `src/cmd/t_server.cc:638`).
+4. Snapshot start calls `writer.progress_fused_executor()` during preparation/freeze/mark (`src/snapshot/snapshot.cc:284`). With overlap armed this hook calls `fused_coarse_pass()` on the same executor (`src/core/genthread.cc:203`).
+5. That re-enters task draining while the older outer batch is still held. The ordinary drain takes queue entries before execution and retires them around its callback (`src/core/thread.h:609`). The pre-filler exceptional-state check only sees snapshot state that already existed before the callback (`src/core/ex_loop.h:463`); a BGSAVE started inside the callback is later than that check.
+
+The resulting concern is that younger work, including later work on the same connection, can be drained while earlier work remains in the outer batch. That is an ordering/RYOW and snapshot-cut risk, not a complaint about unrelated cross-client ordering. It needs a directed counterexample that forces this callback and proves the window opened. The earlier overlap-design report independently records guarding MULTI clients against this same recursion; its guard is not present in the current WB capture/filler shown above. No unrelated fix or speculative guard was added in O7.
